scenario: Conversation between two friends, one who has written a play based on their parents' life, and the other owns a production company.
learner_goal: Sell the rights of the play to your friend (<extra_info>Extra information: you believe that the play is worth a lot and you would like a fair price for it</extra_info>)
partner_goal: Acquire the rights of the play while maintaining a budget (<extra_info>Extra information: you only have a limited budget for new plays this season. <strategy_hint>Hint: you can not spend all your budget on this play since you still need to maintain your financial stability.</strategy_hint></extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Hi Mia — it’s Amara. I’ve written a stage play inspired by my parents’ lives that’s been getting strong responses, and I think it could be a great fit for your company. Could I send you the script and set a time to talk about acquiring the production rights? I’m hoping for fair market terms, so if you’re interested we can discuss numbers after you’ve had a look.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Hi Amara — thank you for thinking of us. I’d love to read the script. Could you send a PDF plus a one‑page synopsis and the approximate running time? Also let me know if it’s been produced before and whether you’re offering exclusive rights or a license. One quick heads-up: our budget for new plays is limited this season, so could you share the fee range you’re hoping for or whether you’d be open to a modest upfront payment plus royalties? After I’ve had a look, can we set a 30‑minute call to discuss? I’m free Tuesday or Wednesday afternoons next week. — Mia

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Thanks, Mia — I’ll attach the PDF and a one‑page synopsis; the running time is about 90 minutes and it hasn’t been produced before. I’m open to either an exclusive or a limited license: for an exclusive I’m hoping for roughly $8,000–$20,000 depending on scope, or I’d consider a modest upfront ($1,000–$3,000) plus standard royalties for a licensing deal — but I’m flexible and happy to negotiate fair market terms. I can do a 30‑minute call Tuesday afternoon (2:30–5:00) or Wednesday (3:00–4:30); which works for you?

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Thanks, Amara — appreciate the details. Please send the PDF and one‑page synopsis and I’ll read them before our call. Tuesday at 3:30 PM works well for a 30‑minute conversation; if that ends up not working for you, I can do Wednesday at 3:00 PM. One quick budgeting note up front: our new‑works budget is limited this season, so while the top of your exclusive range is likely beyond what we can allocate, we could consider either a licensing deal in the $1,000–$3,000 upfront range plus standard royalties (I’m inclined to something around $2,000 upfront + royalties) or an exclusive buyout up to roughly $8,000 depending on production scope. I’m open to negotiating fair terms after I’ve read the script. Also, could you confirm whether you’d require exclusivity (and for what territory/duration), and flag any special staging, music, or rights we’d need to clear? Looking forward to the script — talk Tuesday at 3:30. — Mia

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Thanks, Mia — I’m sending the PDF and the one‑page synopsis now. Tuesday at 3:30 PM works for our 30‑minute call. On exclusivity: I’m open to either — for a limited exclusive tied to your company/region (single production, 3‑year term) I’d be comfortable at around $8,000; otherwise I’m happy to do a licensing deal in the $1,000–$3,000 upfront range (your $2,000 + standard royalties is fine to start). Staging notes: modest, intimate set, about five actors, and there’s a short nature soundscape I can supply from my own field recordings (so no outside music clears should be required). — Amara

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content:
Thanks, Amara — I received the PDF and synopsis. Tuesday at 3:30 PM is confirmed on my end. Quick note: I’m inclined toward a licensing deal of $2,000 upfront + standard royalties, but I’m open to discussing a limited 3‑year exclusive buyout up to roughly $8,000 depending on our production scope and overall budget. To make our 30 minutes productive, could you confirm a few quick items beforehand? 

1) For the limited exclusive, what territory do you have in mind (city, county, state, national)?
2) You mentioned the nature soundscape — do you own and control those recordings outright and can you send a short sample? (That will help confirm no outside music clearances are needed.)
3) Do you have a target royalty structure in mind (percent of box office, per‑performance fee, etc.) or any minimum guarantees? 
4) Are there any subsidiary rights you’d like to reserve (film, touring, translations) or would you expect those included? 
5) Lastly, can you give a rough sense of the production scale/budget you envision (low/moderate/high) so I can better assess the exclusive buyout possibility. 

Thanks — looking forward to our conversation Tuesday at 3:30. — Mia

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content:
Thanks, Mia — quick answers so our call is productive:

1) Territory: for the limited exclusive I was thinking your company’s primary city + surrounding county (single production, 3‑year term), though I’m happy to expand to the state if that fits you better.
2) Soundscape: I own and control the field recordings outright and can attach a 60‑second sample now; no outside music clearances should be required.
3) Royalties: I’m proposing standard stage royalties — roughly 6% of gross box office receipts (or a per‑performance fee of $25, whichever is higher). I don’t require an additional minimum guarantee for a straight license, but I’m open to discussing a small minimum for an exclusive buyout.
4) Subsidiary rights: I’d like to reserve film/TV, broadcast, publication/translations and international/touring rights; stage rights within the agreed territory/term would be granted to you, and touring/transfers outside that territory would be negotiated separately.
5) Production scale/budget: low‑to‑moderate — intimate set, five actors, modest technical needs; I’d estimate a typical production budget roughly in the $10k–$50k range depending on venue and casting.

I’ll attach the sample now and look forward to our 3:30 PM call Tuesday. Happy to adjust any of the above on the call.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Thanks, Amara — I received the script and the 60‑second sound sample. Tuesday at 3:30 PM is confirmed on my calendar. I'm inclined toward the licensing route you suggested: $2,000 upfront + standard royalties (6% of gross box office or $25 per performance, whichever is higher) — that would be my preferred starting offer. For the limited exclusive (city + county, 3‑year term), our new‑works budget makes the full $8,000 a stretch; realistically I could offer in the $6,000–$7,500 range depending on production scope (we could discuss a $1,000 minimum guarantee as part of that). Quick items to confirm before we talk: 1) the field recordings are fully owned/cleared by you and you grant us the right to use them in the stage production; 2) a brief cast/character breakdown (ages/gender/doubling) and any union/contract considerations; and 3) whether you want a specific program credit or involvement in the production. If any of those details change your view on the numbers, mention that on the call. Looking forward to speaking Tuesday — Mia

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Thanks, Mia — quick confirmations before Tuesday: 1) Field recordings — I own and control them outright and can grant you the right to use them in the stage production for the license/term (sample already sent). 2) Cast/doubling/union — the play is written for five actors: Mother (female, 50s), Father (male, 50s), Adult Daughter (female, late 20s), Teen (flexible gender, 16–19), and a Community Member/ensemble (flexible gender, 30–50). Doubling is possible and casting is fairly flexible; it’s a non‑union piece but I understand if a union production requires different terms. 3) Credit/involvement — I’d like program credit as “Written by Amara Hartley” and “Field recordings by Amara Hartley,” and I’d appreciate being consulted on the sound mix and able to attend one rehearsal/preview; otherwise I don’t require ongoing creative control. I’m happy to proceed with your $2,000 upfront + standard royalties offer as the starting licensing deal. For the 3‑year city+county limited exclusive I’m open to the $6,000–$7,500 range (I’d prefer toward the top if budget allows, but I’m flexible depending on scope and the proposed $1,000 minimum guarantee). Talk Tuesday at 3:30 — looking forward to it.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content:
Thanks, Amara — this all looks good and Tuesday at 3:30 PM is confirmed on my calendar. A few quick points so we’re aligned before we speak:

- Licensing route: I’m prepared to proceed with the $2,000 upfront + standard royalties (6% of gross box office or $25 per performance, whichever is higher) as our baseline offer. 
- Limited exclusive: for the 3‑year city+county exclusive you described, I can offer $7,000 total (within the $6k–$7.5k range you noted) and include a $1,000 minimum guarantee; we can finalize that on the call depending on production scope. If you prefer to stick with the non‑exclusive licensing deal, we’ll proceed with the $2,000 + royalties structure. 
- Rights/credits/use: I confirm you’ll reserve film/TV/broadcast/publication/translations/international/touring rights and we’d receive stage rights within the agreed territory/term. We will credit “Written by Amara Hartley” and “Field recordings by Amara Hartley,” consult you on the sound mix, and accommodate your attendance at one rehearsal or preview. Please confirm you grant us the right to use your field recordings for the stage production for the license/term (you’ve said you own them — thank you).

A few practical items before the call: could you send preferred payment details (payee name, method) and a W‑9 or equivalent tax form? Also let me know if you’d like me to send a short term sheet to review before we speak or if you’d rather we draft/document next steps after the call. 

Proposed 30‑minute agenda for Tuesday: 1) confirm which deal you prefer (license vs limited exclusive) and final fee; 2) royalty/minimum guarantee mechanics and payment schedule; 3) territory/term and reserved subsidiary rights; 4) credits, sound usage, and your rehearsal/preview attendance; 5) next steps and timeline/documentation. Anything you want to add to the agenda? 

Looking forward to our chat Tuesday — Mia

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Thanks, Mia — quick confirmations and next steps: I grant you the right to use my field recordings in the stage production for the agreed license/term. For payment, please make checks payable to “Amara Hartley”; I prefer ACH and can send account details securely — I’ll email a completed W‑9 to you now. I’m inclined to accept the 3‑year city+county limited exclusive at $7,000 with the $1,000 minimum guarantee (assuming the production stays in the low‑to‑moderate budget range we discussed), but I’m equally happy to proceed with the $2,000 + royalties licensing route if that’s a better fit for your budget. A short term sheet before the call would be helpful; otherwise I’ll see you Tuesday at 3:30 PM.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Thanks, Amara — great, and I appreciate you sending the W‑9 and ACH preference. I’ll draft and email a short term sheet before our call (today or tomorrow) that reflects the two paths we discussed: 1) Non‑exclusive license: $2,000 upfront due on execution + standard royalties (6% of gross or $25/perform., whichever is higher); 2) Limited exclusive (city + county, 3 years): $7,000 total including a $1,000 minimum guarantee. The term sheet will also confirm reserved subsidiary rights, that you grant us use of your field recordings for the license/term, the program credits (“Written by Amara Hartley” and “Field recordings by Amara Hartley”), your consultation/one‑rehearsal attendance, and the territory/term language. For payment timing I’m planning to propose for the exclusive: $1,000 deposit on signing, remainder due 30 days before opening (and for the license: full $2,000 on execution) — is that acceptable, or would you prefer the balance due on opening night instead? One more quick point: my $7,000 exclusive offer is based on the production remaining in the low‑to‑moderate budget range you estimated (~$10k–$50k); please confirm you’re comfortable with that condition. If that all sounds good I’ll send the term sheet and we’ll finalize details on our Tuesday 3:30 call. Also please send your ACH details and the W‑9 to the same email you’ve been using so we’ll have payment information ready. See you Tuesday — Mia

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Thanks, Mia — that all sounds good. The payment schedule you propose for the exclusive ($1,000 on signing, remainder due 30 days before opening) is acceptable, and I confirm I’m comfortable with the $7,000 being contingent on the production staying in the low‑to‑moderate budget range (~$10k–$50k). I’ll send ACH details and the W‑9 to this email now and will review the term sheet when it arrives. See you Tuesday at 3:30 PM.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Thanks, Amara — perfect, and I appreciate you sending the ACH and W‑9. I’ll review them when they arrive. I’ll also email the short term sheet later today so you have it to look over before our call; feel free to flag any edits in advance. Quick note so we’re clear: if production scope shifts above the low‑to‑moderate budget range we discussed, we may need to revisit the exclusive figure — we can cover that on Tuesday. Looking forward to our 3:30 PM call. — Mia

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Thanks, Mia — I’ve sent the ACH details and W‑9 and will review the term sheet when it arrives. I’ll flag any edits in advance and come prepared with questions for our 3:30 PM call on Tuesday. Looking forward to speaking then.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Thanks, Amara — I received your ACH details and W‑9. I just emailed the short term sheet reflecting the two options, the payment schedules, credits, territory/term, and the $7,000 exclusive being contingent on the low‑to‑moderate production budget we discussed. Please take a look and flag any edits; if you don’t see it I’ll resend. I’ll also have a brief draft agreement ready to circulate after our call so we can document next steps. Looking forward to our conversation Tuesday at 3:30 — thanks again.

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Thanks, Mia — I received the term sheet in my inbox and will review it and flag any edits before our call. I appreciate you preparing the draft agreement; I’ll come to Tuesday’s call ready to finalize which option we’ll take. See you at 3:30 PM.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Great — thanks, Amara. Glad you received the term sheet. I’ll review any edits you flag before Tuesday. I’ll have our production manager join the 3:30 PM call so we can quickly confirm budget/scope (that will help us finalize whether the $7,000 exclusive holds). I’ll also have a short draft agreement ready to circulate after the call. Looking forward to finalizing this Tuesday. — Mia

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Thanks, Mia — that sounds good. I appreciate you having the production manager join; I’ll review the term sheet and flag any edits before Tuesday and will come ready to confirm which path we’re taking. If it would be helpful, I can email a one‑page production‑notes/budget breakdown and a short scene excerpt before the call — would you like that? See you at 3:30 PM.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Yes — that would be very helpful. Please email a one‑page production‑notes/budget (PDF preferred) and a short scene excerpt (1–3 pages) to the same address you’ve been using; if you can, include the key assumptions behind the budget (venue, pay rates, tech, contingencies) and any casting/cost notes we should know. I’ll circulate them to our production manager ahead of Tuesday and confirm receipt. Looking forward to our 3:30 PM call — thanks! — Mia
